summary: Thank you starts with a flat hand at the chin and moves out toward the person you're thanking. It's often shortened to a quick touch-and-move in casual signing.
movement: Fingertips touch the chin, then the hand moves forward and down
steps: Touch the fingertips of a flat hand to your chin, palm facing you.
Move the hand forward and slightly down, toward the person you're thanking.
Let your face match. A small nod and a warm expression complete the sign.
note: THANK-YOU and GOOD start the same way, with the hand at the chin. GOOD lands on the other palm; THANK-YOU moves out toward the person. If you forget which is which, think about who the sign is aimed at.
mistakes: Blowing a kiss. The hand touches the chin, not the lips, and moves out flat rather than puckering.
Ending with the hand still at your chin. The movement outward is what makes it thank you.

faq.q: How do I say 'thank you very much'?
faq.a: Sign THANK-YOU with both hands at once, or make the movement bigger and slower with a stronger expression. There's also a dedicated clip for THANK-YOU-VERY-MUCH in the Greetings category.

faq.q: Is thank you the same as good?
faq.a: They start the same, but no. GOOD lands on your other palm. THANK-YOU moves out toward the person.
